correctness.rationale: Radial orthogonality gives the beta quotient; the substitution t/(1-t) gives the Tricomi integral, taking its Abel limit after the ordinary oscillatory integral is justified. With v=1/(1-t) the tail tends to zero by integration by parts exactly when beta=lambda−gamma>−2; for beta≤−2 the integrals over [R,R+pi] have magnitude asymptotic to 2R^(−beta−2), violating Cauchy convergence. Independently checked the saddle: on the small radius r connector the angular integral of the damping is O(r), giving O(r^(beta+2)); the outer connector and real remainder at m^(−1/3) are O(poly(m) exp(−c m^(2/3))). On u=w x/sqrt(m), w=exp(−i pi/4), the leading exponent is −sqrt(m) w(x+1/x); the correction i x²/2 is imaginary and the remaining real correction is uniformly bounded up to the contour cutoff. Localization at x=1 gives the complex Gaussian sqrt(pi/w), the stated power and the exp(i/2) factor. The counting constant follows by squeezing around k=(log(1/s))²/2 using log(1/|mu_k|)~sqrt(2k); an arbitrary relative o(1) does not alone imply monotonicity, but monotonicity is unnecessary and also follows from I_(m+1)(beta)=I_m(beta)−I_m(beta+1) and I_m(beta+1)/I_m(beta)~w/sqrt(m), with the beta-normalizer ratio only 1+O(1/m). For the tail use one integration by parts: before dividing by B(m,lambda+1) it is O(eps^(beta+2)) when m eps≤1 and O(m^(−beta−2)) when m eps≥1, using exponential bounds on (1−u)^(m−1). This proves the uniform upper rate for gamma≤1. At m eps→lambda+1, a second integration by parts after scaling u=eps x makes the remainder O(eps^(beta+3)), giving the stated positive lower constant. Diagonal convergence on the dense finite-mode space plus uniform bounds proves strong convergence at gamma=1; the diverging norms preclude strong convergence above it. Compactness and all Schatten inclusions follow from spectral decay and harmonic dimensions.
residual_risks: The asymptotics are at fixed d, lambda, gamma. The frozen finite diagnostics are illustrative (the cutoff samples in the script reach gamma=1, not gamma>1); the third regime rests on the analytic lower bound, not on those diagnostics.

evidence: Hagger et al. give uniform boundedness under the weak box-average condition (2.4), strong radial truncation in Theorem 2.4, and compactness under its vanishing version in Theorem 2.5.

Each near-boundary box has comparable depth h; radial integration by parts bounds the ratio of its partial oscillatory integral to weighted box volume by O(h^(1−gamma)), including for an interval cut at a radial threshold.
Rozenblum compares cancellation against the modulus for a different, rapidly oscillating radial sine. The critical-winding Resultary record varies an angular phase rather than a radial amplitude.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general average results give strong convergence for gamma≤1 and compactness for gamma<1; applying the norm bound to the tail also gives the upper rate for gamma<1. They do not give the high-degree lower estimate, critical failure of norm convergence, or compact mode-extension alongside divergent truncations.
